How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the
following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted, and comment for agenda
items 3 and 4 is combined.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the
City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three minutes per person (six
minutes if using an interpreter) per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be
shortened to allow all speakers to address the City Council. Please note that interactions
between the City Council, City staff, and the public during meetings are subject to the City’s
Rules of Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public comment
form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration, but will
not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to
Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Via Zoom or Telephone: “Raise your hand” - Members of the public may speak by using the
“Raise Hand” function during the public comments portion, if on Zoom or telephone. Staff will
unmute speakers participating via Zoom or telephone and announce your name when it is your
time to speak. When calling in using a telephone press *9 to raise your hand and press *6 to
unmute yourself when called. Public Comments via Zoom or Telephone shall follow the
same rules as In-Person.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 26-51 APPROVING NON-EXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE
  AGREEMENTS FOR TOWING SERVICES WITH NAVARRO’S TOWING AND
  HENRY’S TOWING AND RECOVERY, INCORPORATED

  On June 16, 2020, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 664 establishing a
  non-exclusive vehicle towing franchise. On August 17, 2026, San Gabriel Police
  Department issued Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 26-14 for towing and
  storage services with the purpose of increasing the number of qualified towing
  and storage companies available to serve the department. Increasing the
  available number of qualified towing companies to a police department can
  significantly improve operational, financial, and public services. Additionally,
  having multiple towing companies available helps provide greater flexibility
  and more timely services to police personnel when needed. The City received
  five (5) responses to RFP 26-14. The responsive companies are Foothill Towing,
  Dickson’s Towing, Helms & Hill, Navarro’s Towing, and Henry’s Towing. The
  non-exclusive franchise agreements are for a term of three (3) years with two
  (2) one-year optional renewals.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 6, 2026  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. 26-51 to establish the franchise fee and approve the
  form Tow Service Agreement.

  2. Grant a non-exclusive towing service franchise to Navarro’s Tow and Henry’s
  Towing & Recovery, Incorporated.

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a Tow Services Agreement between
  the City and each approved tow service operator.

  D. CYBERSECURITY SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT WITH DARKTRACE FOR A
  THIRTY-SIX-MONTH PERIOD IN THE AMOUNT OF $148,078.93

  Cybersecurity is essential to ensuring the uninterrupted operation of City
  services. While existing measures provide a foundation of protection, the
  sensitive nature of the Police Department’s Information Technology Network –
  as well as compliance requirements from the State and Federal Department of
  Justice – necessitate an additional layer of security. The City has utilized
  Darktrace to provide that extra layer of cybersecurity for the Police Department
  and City Hall over the past 36 months, during which the platform has
  demonstrated consistent value in threat detection and response.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve staff’s recommendation for a sole-source approach and award a
  thirty-six-month subscription agreement with Darktrace in the total amount
  of $148,078.93 ($49,359.64 per year) for enhanced cybersecurity protection
  of the Police Department and City Hall Information Technology networks.

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Product Order Form (Quote Ref.
  Q-282292) and any related documents on behalf of the City.

  E. PURCHASE OF A BRAUN CHIEF XL AMBULANCE AND RELATED
  EQUIPMENT IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $415,000 [RESOLUTION
  NO. 26-13]

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 6, 2026  4
   The San Gabriel Fire Department is seeking approval to purchase a Braun Chief
  XL Rescue Ambulance as a replacement for a 2012 ambulance. The majority of
  the purchase is funded by an award from Senator Sasha Renée Pérez with
  supplemental funds included for ambulance replacement in the approved Fiscal
  Year 2026-2027 budget. Shop No. 266 is a 2012 Ford Chassis ambulance that
  was in service for five years as a frontline response vehicle and has been used
  as a reserve ambulance for the past seven years.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-13 authorizing
  the Fire Chief to purchase a Braun Rescue Ambulance and related equipment
  as detailed in this Staff Report, in an amount not to exceed a total of $415,000
  for the entire project.

  F. PURCHASE OF THREE (3) FIRE DEPARTMENT STAFF VEHICLES IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $223,800 [RESOLUTION NO. 26-52]

  The San Gabriel Fire Department utilizes a variety of vehicles in its fleet to meet
  emergency response and administrative responsibilities. The Division Chiefs are
  assigned vehicles with communications and emergency response equipment to
  effectively respond to and assume command of large-scale incidents that occur
  in the City, and to commute to and from various meetings and conferences.
  The new vehicles will replace a 2014 Toyota Highlander, a 2012 Toyota
  Highlander and a 2018 Ford Explorer that was recycled from the Police Fleet. In
  addition, a 2021 Ford Explorer will be re-assigned to the Fire Prevention Bureau.
  Existing vehicles will be returned to the San Gabriel Public Works Fleet Division
  for re-assignment or removal from inventory subject to the City of San Gabriel
  policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-52,
  authorizing the Fire Chief to purchase three (3) RAM 1500 trucks complete with
  shell and bed deck system.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 6, 2026  5
   G. ACCEPTANCE OF STATE BUDGET AWARD IN THE AMOUNT OF $350,000
  FROM THE OFFICE OF SENATOR SASHA RENÉE PÉREZ [RESOLUTION NO.
  26-53]

  In an effort to meet the increasing requests for Fire Department services and to
  plan for continuity of operations and continued growth in the future, staff has
  spent a considerable amount of time identifying revenue sources outside of
  traditional funding streams. Over the past several years, relationships between
  Fire Department Command Staff and Federal and State elected officials have
  been developed, leading to opportunities that are beneficial to both the City of
  San Gabriel and surrounding communities. The City of San Gabriel has been
  awarded budget funds from Senator Sasha Renée Pérez in the amount of
  $350,000 to purchase an additional Rescue Ambulance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 26-53 to approve
  the following:

  1. Amend the estimated revenue (account 186-3225) and appropriation
  (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants Fund’ by $350,000 and increase estimated
  revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special Projects Funds
  (account 124-761-57-99-304) by $350,000.

  2. Authorize the Fire Chief or designee to accept the grant and purchase the
  items and services needed to complete the project under the City’s
  purchasing policy.

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute the subrecipient agreement between
  the City and the State of California.

  H. APPROVAL OF FIREWORKS DISPLAY PERMIT FOR GABRIELINO HIGH
  SCHOOL ON OCTOBER 23, 2026

  Fireworks & Stage FX America, on behalf of Gabrielino High School, has made
  application to the San Gabriel Fire Department for a fireworks permit to conduct
  a fireworks display on school property on October 23, 2026. The display is to
  begin at 8:00 P.M. and last for approximately two minutes. No more than ten
  (10) low-level (maximum altitude of 125 feet) aerial devices are to be utilized
  for the display. Pursuant to San Gabriel Municipal Code Title IX Sections 96.21

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 6, 2026  6
   – 96.23, City Council approval is required to issue a permit on approval and
  recommendation of the Fire Chief for pyrotechnic displays.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Fire Chief or Deputy Fire
  Marshal to issue a fireworks permit to Fireworks & Stage FX America, on behalf
  of Gabrielino High School, contingent on meeting the conditions of the
  application.

  I. 2026 CITY COUNCIL MEETING SCHEDULE ADJUSTMENT AND 2027 CITY
  COUNCIL MEETING SCHEDULE

  The City Council is scheduled to meet regularly on the first and third Tuesdays
  of each month. At the end of each year, the City Council schedules the meetings
  for the year ahead.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the cancellation of the
  November 3, 2026, regular City Council meeting due to the General Municipal
  Election of the same date, and approve the 2027 City Council meeting schedule.

  J. APPROVAL OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH RKA
  CONSULTING GROUP FOR ENGINEERING PLAN CHECKING SERVICES IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $250,000

  Approximately five years ago, the City of San Gabriel awarded a professional
  services agreement to RKA Consulting Group to provide engineering plan
  checking services. RKA Consulting Group has satisfactorily performed these
  services during the agreement term. With the agreement term ending this year,
  the City issued a new Request for Proposals (RFP) to solicit qualified firms to
  provide continued engineering plan checking services. As a professional
  service, the selection of the engineering plan checking services is based on
  demonstrated competence and qualifications as well as responsiveness to the
  RFP’s directions/requirements rather than solely on the lowest proposed cost.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 6, 2026  7
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve a Professional Services Agreement with RKA Consulting Group for
  Engineering Plan Checking Services in an amount not to exceed $250,000
  for the initial two-year term;

  2. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute the agreement; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or designee to exercise up to three additional
  one-year extensions, subject to satisfactory performance and continued
  need for the services.

  K. MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH IRIS INTERACTIVE
  FOUNDATION FOR USE OF THE GRAPEVINE ARBOR FOR FREE
  COMMUNITY EVENTS

  IRIS Interactive Foundation (IRIS) is a Southern California 501(c)3 operated by a
  team of approximately 80 volunteers. IRIS seeks to host events that focus on
  anime and gaming with live in-character performers, original story experiences,
  themed food and beverage, and interactive activity stations at the Grapevine
  Arbor. These events are free to attend, though food and merchandise is
  available for purchase. IRIS hosted two events at the Grapevine Arbor previously
  and both drew a large crowd. IRIS would like to offer these events on an
  ongoing basis and develop a partnership with the City of San Gabriel. Since the
  primary draw for these events is teens and young adults, which is not typically
  a demographic seen at other community events, staff agrees that this may
  prove to be beneficial and enhance the offerings to the San Gabriel community.
  Additionally, the events have potential economic benefits for the Mission
  District.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 6, 2026  8
   1. Approve the Memorandum of Understanding with IRIS Interactive
  Foundation; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign the Memorandum of Understanding.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. STREET NAME SIGN REPLACEMENT SPECIAL MAINTENANCE PROJECT -
  DISCUSSION AND POTENTIAL PURCHASE

  Staff replace various street name signs throughout each year, but many are over
  15 years old and highly faded. In response to this, $200,000 of additional
  funding for street name sign maintenance was included in the Fiscal Year (FY)
  2025-2026 Adopted Budget to purchase sufficient street name signs for staff
  to install city-wide. The funding was carried over into the FY 2026-2027
  Adopted Budget while staff inspected existing sign locations and conditions to
  estimate necessary quantities. Based on questions and debate around the
  current street name sign design, including how sign color affects its useful
  lifespan due to fading in particular, the City Council has been presented with
  alternative recommendations on how to potentially proceed.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project is
  determined to be Categorially Exempt per CEQA Section 15301 – the project
  consists of minor alterations to existing public right-of-way facilities. No potential
  for significant impacts to the environment is anticipated in this project.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1a. Review and discuss the street name sign design and specifications;

  2a. Approve the purchase of street name signs from Pacific Products and
  Services, LLC as the lowest qualified bidder;

  3a. Adopt Resolution No. 26-50 appropriating $51,416 from the Measure R
  fund to Account number 124-800-58-97-747;

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 6, 2026  9
   4a. Authorize the City Manager to issue a purchase order in the amount of
  $228,560 for the supply and delivery of the street name signs; and

  5a. Authorize separate purchase order in the amount of $22,856 for a 10%
  contingency, for a total authorized amount of $251,416.

  Or:

  1b. Review and discuss the street name sign design and specifications; and

  2b. Provide direction to staff on alternate courses of action to explore regarding
  sign design and specifications.
